prompt: We want to waive shipping fees for an order if ANY of these are true: the order total is above a threshold, the customer has an active premium membership, or they used a valid promo code. Checking the promo code requires calling an external validation service which is slow, so we want to avoid that call whenever possible. How should I structure this?
expected_output: A solution using OrRule (or equivalent short-circuiting logic) with the expensive promo-code check ordered last, and an explanation of why that ordering matters.
expectations: The three checks are combined with OR-like (any-one-passes) semantics
The expensive/slow promo-code check is explicitly ordered last, after the two cheap checks
The solution states or proves that the expensive check is skipped once an earlier check already passes
A test or explicit verification proves the skip actually happens (e.g. a call-counter), not just an assumption that ordering alone guarantees it
The explanation names *why* evaluation order matters (short-circuiting), not just that it happens to work
